IEE Colloquium on Television Automation: Todays Technology, Tomorrow's Opportunities
abstract: Two systems that are in use at Channel Four are described. The on-air presentation of programmes is handled by the Computer Aided Transmission System (CATS). The dissemination of on-air and advance schedule information to the regional Independent Television companies is via a system called IDENT which encodes this information as a teletext signal. CATS is configured to control VTR operations, the presentation mixer, and IDENT.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Automation: Todays Technology, Tomorrow's Opportunities
abstract: Concentrates on some of the aspects of BASYS International's RMS system, namely the Resource Scheduling Module (RSM) and the Production Modules. The RSM focuses on three aspects of the scheduling process: programme management, facilities and equipment management, and personnel management. The Production Module deals with lines booking, input recording and edit suite assignment. It allows the scheduling and booking of incoming and outgoing feeds. The system checks for conflicts and notifies the manager for resolution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Television production in the 1990s: many channels for efficient producers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Automation: Todays Technology, Tomorrow's Opportunities
abstract: In the 1990s, viewers will receive the benefit of hundreds of distribution channels on cable and DBS. To be viable, services that populate these new channels must find the least expensive production methods. This will free funds to invest in the highest quality programming necessary to define their new video niche. As audiences fractionalize, revenue declines, and debt increases, many traditional television organizations will find it necessary to reduce their production and operating costs if they are to maintain content quality and financial viability. Full production automation and the use of consumer grade equipment will play significant roles as the new and traditional television organizations struggle to prosper in the next decade.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Television newsroom automation: the ultimate specification
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Automation: Todays Technology, Tomorrow's Opportunities
abstract: Specifies some of the priorities, and systems, that end users would like to see on offer in years to come. The aim is to maximise the cost, time and efficiency of a total news system. There are two main established newsroom computer system manufacturers. The totally automated newsroom must have complete duplication and considerable redundancy in key areas to accommodate the inevitable equipment or partial system failure. Partial breakdown is to be expected, and the complimentary partial manual override has to be allowed for in the same way.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An outline of an ITV transmission system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Automation: Todays Technology, Tomorrow's Opportunities
abstract: Outlines the transmission facilities of HTV, the independent TV contractor for Wales and the West of England. The computerised control system offers a manually assisted function in addition to fully automatic modes. The host computer exercises control over the presentation switcher, the LMS and the electronic stills store.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automation systems: today's technology, tomorrow's opportunities (broadcasting)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Automation: Todays Technology, Tomorrow's Opportunities
abstract: The approach taken by Sony to tackle the problem of the variety of system applications is discussed. They chose to build their systems around both Betacam SP (an analogue component format) and D-2 digital composite. The system architecture implemented enabled maximum distribution of intelligence and system flexibility, both in terms of the hardware and the software. A dedicated host computer interface is provided at the application level for the purpose of integrating the multicassette system with the news room, master control or traffic management systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Automation of broadcasting activities in BBC news and current affairs
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Automation: Todays Technology, Tomorrow's Opportunities
abstract: The BBC has been using automation for some long time and in many ways the normal process of introducing new equipment over the years could be designated in this way. With regard to cameras, BBC television news has used remotely controlled cameras since 1962 both in its main studio for news bulletins and later to control cameras and lighting in remote studies such as Westminster and Broadcasting House. The BBC transmit the 1 O'Clock, 6 O'Clock and 9 O'Clock New programmes as well as hourly daytime bulletins, Newsround and weekend bulletins using remotely controlled cameras. These have the facility to be panned, tilted, zoomed, focussed and in some cases to adjust pedestal height.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Automation: Todays Technology, Tomorrow's Opportunities
abstract: Today the phrase 'automation' is more usually associated with the transmission playout operation and it is this particular application of automation that the article concentrates on. The application of automation in this area is not new. The key reasons behind the renewed interest are twofold. First, market forces now dictate that the broadcaster be as cost-efficient as possible (i.e. cost savings in manpower) and second, the introduction of the new generation of the very large robotic tape libraries that the manufacturers are now producing. There are four major suppliers of these MegaCart Players or MCPs and they are: Ampex ACR225, Odetics Cart Machine, Panasonic MARC, and Sony LMS. All are very similar in concept. They offer the broadcaster the ability to playout several days transmission totally automatically. To do this, they consist of a number of fairly standard VTRs, a basic switcher or matrix to route signals into and out of them, storage bins for upwards of 1000 tape cassettes or cartridges, one or more robotic arms to transfer tapes from their storage bins to the correct VTR and vice versa and a control box or sequencer to prevent the robotic equivalent of hari-kiri.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
